question.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Which of the following pairs could represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y)?$

I. ${f}_{x}(x,y)=2x+5y$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=3x-5y$

II. ${f}_{x}(x,y)=3{x}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=5{y}^{3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$

III. ${f}_{x}(x,y)=x+2y$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=2x-3y$
question.worked_solution:
Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal, that is, ${f}_{xy}(x,y)={f}_{yx}(x,y).$ Let's check if this condition is true for each of our pairs of first-order partial derivatives.

- For the first pair, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+5y)=5, \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x-5y)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

As ${f}_{xy}(x,y)\ne {f}_{yx}(x,y)$, the first pair cannot represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y).$

- For the second pair, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =0+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y, \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{y}^{3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =0-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

As ${f}_{xy}(x,y)\ne {f}_{yx}(x,y)$, the second pair cannot represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y).$

- For the third pair, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+2y)=2, \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x-3y)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

As ${f}_{xy}(x,y)={f}_{yx}(x,y)$, the third pair could represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
